title: AI Papers — arXiv Daily Announcement Batch 2026-11-26
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from cross-list breadth and topical relevance, not readership. Recent-paper citation evidence is limited, and the Semantic Scholar source was unavailable for this collection.

sections.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
sections.abstract: The paper combines pointmap geometric priors with ray-based view selection and local feature aggregation to reconstruct continuous 3D surfaces from unposed images.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report training one model on 9 datasets and zero-shot evaluation on 6 unseen datasets, claiming better geometric accuracy and detail preservation than their baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports zero-shot results on six unseen datasets but does not give dataset names or metric values; the comparison remains the authors' reported evaluation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 1.00, entirely from 4 cross-lists (weighted component 1.00); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: Learning from Natural Images Untangles Number Sense
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a geometric analysis of numerosity and proportion representations and report that visual learning can separate the two representations, improving readout when the quantities conflict.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that increased angular separation and reduced overlap between numerosity and proportion subspaces support more robust readout, and that separation also appears with self-supervised or synthetic-image training.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence concerns the neural-network training and numerical-conflict settings examined in the paper; it does not establish that current deployed vision-language models have human-like number sense.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 1.00 (4 cross-lists; component 1.00), tied for the highest tier; no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
sections.abstract: HumblePRM separately rewards visual scene description and the decision about whether that evidence is sufficient, and the authors report more uncertainty-driven abstention on ambiguous images with roughly unchanged accuracy on clear images.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a lightweight process reward model for separately supervising perception and confidence calibration, and report transfer of the abstention improvement to Gemma 4 E4B.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives no effect sizes or detailed test-set scope, and the reported transfer is to one named model; broad deployment reliability is not established by this abstract.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.75, entirely from 3 cross-lists (component 0.75); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: Two Timescales of Forgetting in Fine-tuning of Language Models: Fast Behavioral Suppression and Slow Representational Drift
sections.abstract: Using controlled grammar models and a natural-language setup, the authors report that fine-tuning suppresses generation of removed rules faster than it erases the internal representations associated with them.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors distinguish a fast change in behavior from slower representational drift during supervised fine-tuning and report analogous effects in a natural-language setup.
sections.unique_caveat: The study's central mechanistic result uses a controlled grammar model; the abstract's natural-language experiment supports an analogy, not a universal claim about forgetting across model families or fine-tuning regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.75, entirely from 3 cross-lists (component 0.75); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
sections.abstract: ClueProbe labels video questions as answerable, guessable, or unanswerable, and the authors report that Video LLMs often perceive clues but fail to judge whether partial evidence supports a guess.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a 1,721-question, 598-video benchmark and report that targeted supervision raises appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported benchmark and fine-tuning evidence is tied to 598 videos and the tested set of 10 models; transfer to other video domains is not established here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists (component 0.50); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
sections.abstract: This systematic review unifies token-level expert gating, query-level model cascades, and task-level agent orchestration under an inspect-then-allocate framing for conditional computation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors synthesize 2,289 studies selected from 13,884 records, identifying computational overhead as a recurring bottleneck and reporting different safeguards across token-, query-, and task-level routing.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a literature synthesis covering studies through September 2026, not a new controlled system comparison; conclusions depend on its study-selection and methodological coding frame.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists (component 0.50); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
sections.abstract: In a study of 90 agent-written Django patches, the authors compare low, medium, and high review effort and report that high effort catches more wrong patches than low effort, while medium effort is non-inferior to high for the preregistered Opus comparison at lower cost.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide preregistered evidence on the cost/quality trade-off of reviewer effort, reporting that Opus at medium effort cost 20% less than high and met their 15-percentage-point non-inferiority margin.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison covers 90 Django patches and three Claude 5.5 models; medium effort was not shown non-inferior for Sonnet or Haiku, limiting generalization beyond this setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists (component 0.50); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.

sections.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
sections.abstract: The authors audit SkillsBench and reanalyse 7,554 public trials, finding that observed negative task-level skill effects were not statistically significant after pooled multiple-testing correction and were vulnerable to run-sampling noise.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a source-code audit and noise-aware reanalysis, including no statistically significant pooled task-level reductions and no significant held-out benefit for the tested skill-gating strategy.
sections.unique_caveat: There were at most three runs per condition in each paired cell, so small effects remain difficult to resolve; the reanalysis is bounded by the public trials and benchmark harnesses examined.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal-file score 0.50, entirely from 2 cross-lists (component 0.50); no paper-specific HF/HN attention match was recorded.
